entityDossier.whatItIs: The Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act of 2023 was submitted by Senator Charles Schumer on 13 July 2023 as Senate Amendment 797 to S. 2226, the FY2024 National Defense Authorization Act, and printed in full in the Congressional Record at pages S2953-S2959. It travelled into the Senate-engrossed NDAA as a freestanding division of fifteen sections. Its enforcement machinery - an independent nine-member Records Review Board, a federal exercise of eminent domain over privately held recovered materials, and a $20,000,000 authorisation - was removed before enactment, leaving only an archiving and postponement regime at sections 1841-1843 of Public Law 118-31.
entityDossier.whyImplicated: This is the only text ever adopted by a chamber of the United States Congress that legislates on the express premise that recovered technologies of unknown origin and biological evidence of non-human intelligence exist and are held in part by private entities. Its definitions are not rhetorical: 'controlling authority' is defined to include any commercial company, academic institution, or private sector entity in physical possession of such material, and 'legacy program' is defined to reach commercial, academic and private-sector reverse-engineering endeavours predating enactment. Six senators including the Majority Leader and the Vice Chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee put their names to a finding that records exist which have been shielded from mandatory declassification review by Atomic Energy Act exemptions and an over-broad reading of transclassified foreign nuclear information. The bill then directs the Federal Government to seize that material by eminent domain and hand it to a board explicitly barred from containing anyone who has ever worked on a legacy program. The provisions that would have moved custody, compelled testimony and paid for the effort are precisely the provisions that did not survive conference - which is the single most informative fact on this node.
entityDossier.narrative:
On 13 July 2023 the Senate Majority Leader rose and submitted an amendment to the defence bill. The Congressional Record entry is flat and procedural - 'SA 797. Mr. SCHUMER (for himself, Mr. Rounds, Mr. Rubio, Mrs. Gillibrand, Mr. Young, and Mr. Heinrich) submitted an amendment intended to be proposed by him to the bill S. 2226 ... which was ordered to lie on the table' - and what follows across seven pages of the Record is the most consequential UAP text in American law.

The structure is deliberately modelled on the President John F. Kennedy Assassination Records Collection Act of 1992: a records collection at the National Archives, a presumption of immediate disclosure, an independent review board with the power to override agency postponement, and a sunset. The differences are where the argument lives. The JFK Act dealt only with paper. This bill deals with objects.

The findings section states the premise. Congress finds that 'Legislation is necessary because credible evidence and testimony indicates that Federal Government unidentified anomalous phenomena records exist that have not been declassified or subject to mandatory declassification review as set forth in Executive Order 13526 ... due in part to exemptions under the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 ..., as well as an over-broad interpretation of "transclassified foreign nuclear information", which is also exempt from mandatory declassification, thereby preventing public disclosure under existing provisions of law.' That is a named legal mechanism of concealment, identified by the Senate, and it points at the Department of Energy and the Restricted Data regime rather than at the Department of Defense alone. The next finding says the Freedom of Information Act 'has proven inadequate.'

The definitions do the load-bearing work. 'Controlling authority' means 'any Federal, State, or local government department, office, agency, committee, commission, commercial company, academic institution, or private sector entity in physical possession of technologies of unknown origin or biological evidence of non-human intelligence.' A commercial company cannot be in physical possession of a thing that does not exist. 'Legacy program' is defined to include 'commercial industry, academic, and private sector endeavors to collect, exploit, or reverse engineer technologies of unknown origin or examine biological evidence of living or deceased non-human intelligence that pre-dates the date of the enactment of this Act.' 'Non-human intelligence' means 'any sentient intelligent non-human lifeform regardless of nature or ultimate origin that may be presumed responsible for unidentified anomalous phenomena or of which the Federal Government has become aware.'

The Review Board provisions establish 'as an independent agency a board to be known as the "Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Review Board"', appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate, nine citizens, without regard to political affiliation. Board staff must be citizens 'of integrity and impartiality who ha[ve] had no previous or current involvement with any legacy program or controlling authority relating to the collection, exploitation, or reverse engineering of technologies of unknown origin or the examination of biological evidence of living or deceased non-human intelligence.' A statute does not write a conflict-of-interest bar against a category of person that Congress believes to be empty.

Then the section that made the bill unpassable. 'The Federal Government shall exercise eminent domain over any and all recovered technologies of unknown origin and biological evidence of non-human intelligence that may be controlled by private persons or entities in the interests of the public good.' Such material 'shall be made available to the Review Board for personal examination and subsequent disclosure determination at a location suitable to the controlling authority of said material.' The Board would then decide whether the material constitutes technologies of unknown origin 'beyond a reasonable doubt', whether it qualifies for postponement, and 'what changes, if any, to the current disposition of said material should the Federal Government make to facilitate full disclosure.' The Board would also 'have access to all testimony from unidentified anomalous phenomena witnesses, close observers and legacy program personnel and whistleblowers within the Federal Government's possession.'

The money section authorised $20,000,000 for fiscal year 2024 and, pending appropriation, permitted the President to use 'such sums as are available for discretionary use.'

What was enacted on 22 December 2023 in Public Law 118-31 is three sections - 1841, 1842 and 1843 - creating the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection at the National Archives, requiring agencies to review, identify, transmit and disclose UAP records, and setting out grounds for postponement. There is no Review Board. There is no eminent domain. There is no authorisation of appropriations. There is no witness-solicitation mandate. The surviving regime asks the original classification authorities that hold the records to identify their own records and to invoke their own postponement grounds, and gives no independent body the power to say no.

That is the argument. The Senate wrote a bill whose operative theory was that the material is held by controlling authorities including private companies, that those companies will not surrender it voluntarily, and that only compulsory acquisition plus an outside board with special access clearances could break the hold. Conference removed compulsion and removed the outside board. What remains is a filing cabinet with the same locks and the same keyholders.

claims.text: S.Amdt. 797 was submitted on 13 July 2023 by Sen. Schumer 'for himself, Mr. Rounds, Mr. Rubio, Mrs. Gillibrand, Mr. Young, and Mr. Heinrich' to S. 2226, and was ordered to lie on the table; the full text is printed at Congressional Record, Vol. 169, No. 120, pages S2953-S2959.

Congressional finding (a)(4): 'Legislation is necessary because credible evidence and testimony indicates that Federal Government unidentified anomalous phenomena records exist that have not been declassified or subject to mandatory declassification review as set forth in Executive Order 13526 ... due in part to exemptions under the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (42 U.S.C. 2011 et seq.), as well as an over-broad interpretation of "transclassified foreign nuclear information", which is also exempt from mandatory declassification, thereby preventing public disclosure under existing provisions of law.'

The definitions section defines 'controlling authority' as 'any Federal, State, or local government department, office, agency, committee, commission, commercial company, academic institution, or private sector entity in physical possession of technologies of unknown origin or biological evidence of non-human intelligence.'

'Legacy program' is defined to include 'commercial industry, academic, and private sector endeavors to collect, exploit, or reverse engineer technologies of unknown origin or examine biological evidence of living or deceased non-human intelligence that pre-dates the date of the enactment of this Act.'

'Non-human intelligence' is defined as 'any sentient intelligent non-human lifeform regardless of nature or ultimate origin that may be presumed responsible for unidentified anomalous phenomena or of which the Federal Government has become aware.'

The Review Board section states: '(a) ESTABLISHMENT.-There is established as an independent agency a board to be known as the "Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Review Board"' and '(1) IN GENERAL.-The President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, shall appoint, without regard to political affiliation, 9 citizens of the United States to serve as members of the Review Board.'

The Review Board staffing section requires that a person appointed to the staff 'shall be a citizen of integrity and impartiality who has had no previous or current involvement with any legacy program or controlling authority relating to the collection, exploitation, or reverse engineering of technologies of unknown origin or the examination of biological evidence of living or deceased non-human intelligence', and requires accelerated grant of 'all necessary special access program clearances'.

The eminent domain provision reads in full: '(a) EXERCISE OF EMINENT DOMAIN.-The Federal Government shall exercise eminent domain over any and all recovered technologies of unknown origin and biological evidence of non-human intelligence that may be controlled by private persons or entities in the interests of the public good.'

The same section provides that '(b) AVAILABILITY TO REVIEW BOARD.-Any and all such material, should it exist, shall be made available to the Review Board for personal examination and subsequent disclosure determination at a location suitable to the controlling authority of said material', and that the Board shall decide 'whether the material examined constitutes technologies of unknown origin or biological evidence of non-human intelligence beyond a reasonable doubt'.

The Board was to 'have access to all testimony from unidentified anomalous phenomena witnesses, close observers and legacy program personnel and whistleblowers within the Federal Government's possession as of and after the date of the enactment of this Act'. The phrase 'legacy program personnel' is statutory text.

The authorisation section provides '$20,000,000 for fiscal year 2024' and adds that 'Until such time as funds are appropriated pursuant to subsection (a), the President may use such sums as are available for discretionary use to carry out this title.'

The National Archives states that it 'has established an "Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection," per sections 1841-1843 of the 2024 National Defense Authorization Act (Public Law 118-31)', and that records received from federal agencies under that Act are accessioned into Record Group 615.

The disclosure machinery enacted in Public Law 118-31 consists only of the NARA records collection at sections 1841-1843; the Review Board, the eminent domain provision, the Review Board witness-access provision and the $20,000,000 authorisation have no enacted counterpart.

claims.text: The provisions removed in conference are exactly the ones that would have moved custody out of the hands of current holders or compelled testimony from legacy-program personnel; the provisions that survived are the ones administered by the same original classification authorities that hold the records.
claims.source: Inference from side-by-side comparison of SA 797 as printed at https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CREC-2023-07-13/pdf/CREC-2023-07-13-pt1-PgS2953.pdf against the enacted secs. 1841-1843 described at https://www.archives.gov/research/topics/uaps

entityDossier.denialPosture: No executive branch office has ever publicly explained why the Review Board and eminent domain sections were removed in conference, and no conference report language identifying an objecting party has been made public. The Department of Defense has never responded on the record to the bill's finding that Atomic Energy Act exemptions and transclassified foreign nuclear information are being used to keep UAP records out of mandatory declassification review.
openQuestions: Which members or agencies asked for the Review Board and eminent domain sections to be struck in the FY2024 NDAA conference, and in what written form was the request made?
Did any executive branch agency submit a Statement of Administration Policy or legislative-referral objection to Division G, and is it retrievable?
Has any agency ever identified a specific record withheld under the 'transclassified foreign nuclear information' exemption that would otherwise be a UAP record?

The Senate text presupposes controlling authorities in physical possession; no controlling authority has ever been named in any public congressional document. Which entities did the drafters have in mind?

Section numbering differs between the Congressional Record print of SA 797 (SEC. __01 through __15) and the engrossed division; the engrossed section numbers used elsewhere on this board should be re-verified against BILLS-118s2226es directly.

The negative claim that no Review Board or eminent domain text survives in Public Law 118-31 was established here by comparison against NARA's description of the enacted sections rather than by a direct full-text search of the enrolled bill, which should be run to close the point.

entityDossier.whatItIs: A hearing of the House Committee on Oversight and Accountability's Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs, held 26 July 2023 at 10:06 a.m. in room 2154 of the Rayburn House Office Building, chaired by Rep. Glenn Grothman. The witnesses were Ryan Graves, David Grusch and retired Commander David Fravor. It was the first congressional hearing at which a former intelligence officer testified under oath that the United States operates a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering programme outside congressional oversight.
entityDossier.whyImplicated: This hearing converted the legacy programme allegation from journalism into sworn testimony before a committee of jurisdiction, and it did so with three specific mechanisms attached: how the programme is hidden (special access programs the witness was denied read-on to), how it is paid for (misappropriation of funds and self-funding), and who holds the material (contractors, described by the witness as 'the metal benders', who are under no requirement to report UAP). Fravor's written statement establishes that the most corroborated modern military encounter was never investigated and the tapes were never collected - an evidentiary vacuum that is itself the artefact. The hearing also demonstrated the ceiling on congressional capability: members were denied a SCIF, no contractor was called, no document production was compelled, and every substantive answer was deferred to a closed session that has never been publicly confirmed to have occurred on these terms. The committee's own wrap-up release then framed the day around pilot reporting and stigma, omitting the crash retrieval testimony entirely.
entityDossier.narrative:
The subcommittee met at 10:06 a.m. on 26 July 2023 in 2154 Rayburn. Present were Representatives Grothman, Gosar, Foxx, Sessions, Biggs, Mace, LaTurner, Armstrong, Perry, Garcia, Moskowitz and Frost; also present, waived on, were Luna, Burlison, Gaetz, Burchett, Comer, Ogles, Langworthy, Raskin and Ocasio-Cortez. The unusual size of the 'also present' list is the first fact about this hearing: members from outside the subcommittee, from both parties, came to sit in.

The second fact came in Burchett's opening. Members, he said, 'were even denied access to a classified briefing in a SCIF prior to this hearing due to the amount of hoops that we had to jump through to grant temporary clearance to witness Grusch, who has knowledge of classified information.' The committee therefore held a public hearing about compartmented programmes without the means to hear about compartmented programmes. Every subsequent deferral in the transcript traces back to that.

Grusch's written opening statement is the core document. He identifies himself as an intelligence officer of fourteen years, a USAF major, and from 2021 to 2023 a GS-15 at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, where he was his agency's co-lead for UAP and transmedium object analysis reporting to the UAP Task Force and then to AARO. He states that he became a whistleblower 'through a PPD-19 Urgent Concern filing with the Intelligence Community Inspector General (ICIG)'. He describes a specific tasking: 'In 2019, the UAPTF director tasked me to identify all Special Access Programs & Controlled Access Programs (SAPs/CAPs) we needed to satisfy our congressionally mandated mission.' And then the sentence the hearing is remembered for: 'I was informed, in the course of my official duties, of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program to which I was denied access to those additional read-on's.' His closing statement calls the programmes he reported the 'Non-Human Reverse Engineering Programs' and predicts their revelation would act as 'an ontological (earth-shattering) shock'.

Under questioning the mechanism claims sharpened. Asked by Rep. Moskowitz how such a programme gets funded, Grusch answered: 'I will give you generalities. I can get very specific in a closed session. But misappropriation of funds and self-fund.' Asked whether that meant money budgeted for one programme goes elsewhere, he said 'Yes. I have specific knowledge of that. Yes.' Asked by Rep. Ocasio-Cortez about interactions between defence contractors and UAP activities, he described 'the contractors, you know, or the metal benders, so to speak, the ones actually doing specific performance on government contracts.' Asked whether those contractors are required to report UAP sightings, he answered: 'In terms of the contractors? Not that I am aware of.' That single exchange is the cleanest statement on the record of the regulatory gap that would allow contractor custody to persist without disclosure.

On where and who, he refused in open session and said the information had gone elsewhere: 'I cannot discuss that publicly, but I did provide that information both to the intel committees and the Inspector General.' Asked by Burchett whether it could be given in a SCIF, he replied 'Sure, if you had the appropriate accesses.' Asked when the government first became aware, he said: 'I like to use the term nonhuman. I do not like to denote origin. Keeps the aperture open both scientifically. Certainly, like I have discussed publicly, previously 1930's.' Asked by Rep. Burlison whether he had personally seen the craft or bodies, he distinguished carefully: on the craft, 'I have to be careful to describe what I have seen firsthand and not in this environment'; on bodies, 'That is something I have not witnessed myself.' The witness is testifying to what he was told and what he documented, not to personal observation, and the transcript is unambiguous that he drew that line himself.

Fravor's written statement supplies the other half. He commanded VFA-41 aboard USS Nimitz in November 2004 and describes the Princeton having tracked the objects on Aegis 'for the previous 2 weeks', descending from above 80,000 feet to 20,000 feet, staying for hours, and going 'straight back up'. His closing judgement is about oversight, not phenomenology: 'even Unacknowledged Waived programs have some level of oversight by the appropriate committee members in the House and Senate and this work that is said to be occurring from Whistleblower testimonies should not be exempt.' And the line that indicts the system: 'What is shocking is that the incident was never investigated, none of my crew were ever questioned, tapes were never taken, and after a couple of days, it turned into a great story to tell friends.'

The official denial was read into the record by a member reciting AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick's prior testimony that there has been 'no credible evidence thus far of extraterrestrial activity' or of 'off-world technology brought to the attention of the office' - a formulation that is a statement about what reached one office, not about what exists.

What the hearing did not produce is as important as what it did. No contractor was called. No document was subpoenaed. The Committee's own wrap-up release, published the same day, lists its Key Takeaways as poor reporting processes and retaliation against pilots, and quotes Graves estimating that only 'somewhere near five percent' of pilot sightings are reported. Crash retrieval, non-human craft and contractor custody do not appear in the committee's summary of its own hearing.

entityDossier.denialPosture: The Department of Defense's position at the hearing was represented only indirectly, through a member quoting AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick's prior testimony that there is 'no credible evidence thus far of extraterrestrial activity' and no 'off-world technology brought to the attention of the office'. No DoD or AARO witness appeared, and the Department made no on-the-record response to the funding-diversion or contractor-custody testimony.
openQuestions: Grusch stated he provided names, locations and documentation to the ICIG and the intelligence committees; none of that material has been published or acknowledged as received in any public committee document.
Whether the classified session Grusch repeatedly offered was ever held on the terms he described, and by which committee.
Which Special Access Programs Grusch identified in his 2019 UAPTF tasking, and whether that tasking product still exists as a retrievable document.

The publicly retrievable copies of the printed record (CHRG-118hhrg53022) and the committee transcript PDF both truncate before the closing rounds of questioning; a complete verified text of the final third of the hearing has not been obtained for this dossier.
No contractor named in open or closed session has been publicly identified, and no committee has issued a subpoena arising from this hearing.

entityDossier.whatItIs: A hearing of the House Oversight Committee's Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, held 9 September 2025 at 10:00 a.m. in HVC-210, chaired by Rep. Anna Paulina Luna with Rep. Jasmine Crockett as ranking member, titled 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection'. The witnesses were Jeffrey Nuccetelli, Senior Chief Petty Officer Alexandro C. Wiggins, George Knapp, Dylan Borland, and minority witness Joe Spielberger of the Project On Government Oversight.
entityDossier.whyImplicated: This is the hearing at which the enquiry stopped being about lights in the sky and became about programme architecture, contracts and custody. Knapp's written testimony placed on the congressional record a detailed account of AAWSAP/BAASS as a prime-contract intelligence programme - fifty cleared investigators, twenty-seven months, a 240,000-case data warehouse still reportedly in agency use, more than a hundred papers never released by DIA - and an account of a negotiated transfer of anomalous material from Lockheed Martin to a private contractor that was agreed and then not completed. Nuccetelli testified that documented, investigated UAP incursions over the National Missile Defense sites at Vandenberg produced records now held by AARO and the FBI, and that a witness was threatened into silence. Wiggins, an active-duty Navy Senior Chief, put multi-sensor Star SAFIRE EO/IR imagery of a transmedium object into the record with time, coordinates and platform. Taken together the hearing establishes that the material, the records and the contracts are locatable - and that the committee could name where they sit without being able to compel their production.
entityDossier.narrative:
The Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets is a creature of the 119th Congress, chaired by Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, and it exists because the 2023 and 2024 hearings demonstrated that a standing subcommittee without access to compartments could not move the file. The 9 September 2025 hearing was held in HVC-210, a House Visitor Center room, with five witnesses and written statements posted by the committee.

Jeffrey Nuccetelli, a former Air Force military police officer with sixteen years of active duty, testified to five UAP incidents at Vandenberg Air Force Base between 2003 and 2005 - the home, as his statement notes, of the National Missile Defense Project, during launches described by the National Reconnaissance Office as 'the most important in twenty-five years.' His formulation of the oversight failure is exact: 'Each incident was witnessed by multiple personnel, documented, investigated, and reported up the chain of command. We sent information up, but no guidance came down.' The 14 October 2003 incursion - Boeing contractors reporting 'a massive, glowing red square silently hovering over two missile defense sites' - is the incident Rep. Luna had raised at the 2023 hearing, and Nuccetelli states that 'Official Air Force records documenting it are now held by AARO and the FBI.' That is a custody claim with two named holders. He also testified that after a later incident 'The witness was later threatened and told to kept quiet about the incident, discouraging further reports.'

Alexandro C. Wiggins, an active-duty Navy Senior Chief Petty Officer with roughly twenty-three years of service, gave the hearing its hardest sensor evidence. On 15 February 2023 at approximately 1915 PST, in the W-291 warning area off Southern California, aboard USS Jackson (LCS-6), a self-luminous Tic-Tac-shaped object was observed emerging from the ocean, joined three similar objects, and all four departed simultaneously with no sonic boom and no conventional propulsion signature. The event was recorded from the Combat Information Center on a Star SAFIRE multi-spectral EO/IR system with visible time and location stamps, the objects were held on radar, and reports were made to the Tactical Action Officer. His statement is careful about what the data does and does not show, and notes an approximate altitude reference of about 22,000 feet reflected in CIC operator conversation.

George Knapp's written testimony is the document that makes this hearing structurally important. He describes AAWSAP as conceived by DIA's Dr. James Lacatski and a colleague, funded through Senator Harry Reid and two other senior senators, and contracted to Robert Bigelow's BAASS, which 'managed to recruit and hire fifty full-time investigators for BAASS, most of them former military or law enforcement, and all of whom were able to qualify for top-secret security clearances.' In twenty-seven months the programme produced 'more than three dozen preliminary reports (DIRDs)' and 'compiled the largest known UFO database - or rather data warehouse - consisting of more than 240,000 case files obtained from multiple other collections, including files from other governments.' That warehouse 'was designed and overseen by Dr. Jacques Vallee and has reportedly been used by U.S. agencies up to the present date.' The programme also produced 'more than 100 highly detailed papers', of which 'None of these 100-plus reports have been released by DIA, though a few have been leaked.'

Knapp then puts two custody claims on the record. First, Lacatski's 2023 statement during Kona Blue discussions with a US senator and an undersecretary of the Department of Homeland Security that 'the U.S. is in possession of a craft of unknown origin and had successfully gained access to its interior', described as having 'a streamlined configuration suitable for aerodynamic flight but no intakes, exhaust, wings, or control surfaces.' Second, and more concrete: 'I have confirmed that Bigelow and a trusted colleague met with and negotiated with a senior executive at Lockheed and hammered out a deal wherein Bigelow's company, BAASS, would receive a quantity of unusual material that Lockheed was safeguarding at a facility in California. A source who was in the room for that discussion has confirmed this.' The material 'contained no unknown element, no unobtanium, but its composition suggested it had been crafted in a zero-gravity environment.' And then: 'The agreement was not completed.'

Knapp also notes, almost in passing, a fact that matters for how this file is now being worked: 'Mr. Grusch now works for Representative Burlison as an advisor on these matters.' The 2023 whistleblower is now congressional staff support on the same subject.

The Russian half of Knapp's testimony - Ministry of Defence documents from his 1993 and 1996 Moscow visits, Colonel Boris Sokolov's decade-long standing collection order 1978-1988, General Igor Maltsev's standing order to disengage, the October 1982 Ukraine missile base incident in which launch displays illuminated and could not be shut down - is presented as material already handed to AAWSAP and BAASS for analysis, with the resulting report 'included in one of those unreleased papers submitted to DIA and still bottled up there.'

The minority witness, Joe Spielberger of the Project On Government Oversight, was there for whistleblower protection rather than phenomena, which is the correct read of the hearing's title. The Task Force's theory is that the bottleneck is not evidence but the legal exposure of the people who hold it.

claims.text: The hearing 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection' was held on 9 September 2025 at 10:00 am in HVC-210 before the House Oversight Committee's Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets.

The witnesses of record were Jeffrey Nuccetelli (U.S. Air Force Veteran), Chief Alexandro Wiggins (UAP Witness), George Knapp (UAP Journalist), Dylan Borland (UAP Witness, U.S. Air Force Veteran) and, as minority witness, Joe Spielberger, Senior Policy Counsel, Project On Government Oversight.

Knapp's written testimony is addressed 'Good morning, Chairwoman Luna, Ranking Member Crockett, and Members of the Task Force', establishing Rep. Anna Paulina Luna as chair and Rep. Jasmine Crockett as ranking member.

Nuccetelli testified to five UAP incidents at Vandenberg Air Force Base between 2003 and 2005, stating: 'Each incident was witnessed by multiple personnel, documented, investigated, and reported up the chain of command. We sent information up, but no guidance came down.'

Nuccetelli testified that the 14 October 2003 incursion began 'when Boeing contractors reported a massive, glowing red square silently hovering over two missile defense sites', and that 'Official Air Force records documenting it are now held by AARO and the FBI.'
Nuccetelli testified that after a subsequent Vandenberg incident 'The witness was later threatened and told to kept quiet about the incident, discouraging further reports.'

Wiggins, an active-duty Navy Senior Chief Petty Officer (Operations Specialist) with approximately 23 years of service, testified to an event on 15 February 2023 at approximately 1915 PST in the W-291 warning area off Southern California aboard USS Jackson (LCS-6), involving a self-luminous Tic-Tac-shaped object emerging from the ocean, linking up with three similar objects, and departing simultaneously with no sonic boom or conventional propulsion signature.

Wiggins testified that the event was recorded inside the Combat Information Center on a Star SAFIRE multi-spectral EO/IR system, that 'The released, stabilized footage includes timestamps, lat/long, and platform readouts consistent with USS Jackson's location in W-291 at the time of the encounter', that the objects were held on radar, and that reports were made to the Tactical Action Officer.

Knapp testified that BAASS, the prime contractor for AAWSAP, 'managed to recruit and hire fifty full-time investigators for BAASS, most of them former military or law enforcement, and all of whom were able to qualify for top-secret security clearances.'

Knapp testified that in its 27-month existence AAWSAP/BAASS produced 'more than three dozen preliminary reports (DIRDs)' and a data warehouse of 'more than 240,000 case files', which 'was designed and overseen by Dr. Jacques Vallee and has reportedly been used by U.S. agencies up to the present date.'

Knapp testified that AAWSAP/BAASS 'also produced more than 100 highly detailed papers focusing on different issues and questions, including studies of the health effects on humans from encounters with UFO/UAP technology. None of these 100-plus reports have been released by DIA, though a few have been leaked.'

Knapp testified that during Kona Blue discussions with a US senator and an undersecretary of the Department of Homeland Security, Dr. James Lacatski revealed that 'the U.S. is in possession of a craft of unknown origin and had successfully gained access to its interior', with 'a streamlined configuration suitable for aerodynamic flight but no intakes, exhaust, wings, or control surfaces.'

Knapp testified: 'I have confirmed that Bigelow and a trusted colleague met with and negotiated with a senior executive at Lockheed and hammered out a deal wherein Bigelow's company, BAASS, would receive a quantity of unusual material that Lockheed was safeguarding at a facility in California. A source who was in the room for that discussion has confirmed this.' He added that the material's 'composition suggested it had been crafted in a zero-gravity environment' and that 'The agreement was not completed.'
Knapp stated on the record that 'Mr. Grusch now works for Representative Burlison as an advisor on these matters.'

entityDossier.denialPosture: No Department of Defense, AARO or DIA witness appeared and no departmental response to the hearing's custody claims - Air Force records held by AARO and the FBI, unreleased DIA papers, the Lockheed material negotiation - has been published. The Department's standing position, restated in AARO's annual reporting, remains that it has found no verifiable evidence of extraterrestrial technology; it has not addressed the specific documentary and contractual allegations made under oath at this hearing.
openQuestions: Whether AARO and the FBI in fact hold the Vandenberg 2003 records Nuccetelli names, and whether either has been asked for them in writing by the Task Force.
The identity of the Lockheed Martin senior executive who negotiated the BAASS material transfer, the California facility involved, and why the agreement was not completed.
Whether the AAWSAP 240,000-case data warehouse designed by Jacques Vallee is still operational, in which agency's hands, and under what contract.
The disposition of the more than 100 unreleased AAWSAP/BAASS papers held by DIA, and whether any FOIA or committee request for them has been answered.
Whether the USS Jackson Star SAFIRE source video and radar tracks were ever transmitted to AARO, and whether the case was adjudicated.

entityDossier.whatItIs: Immaculate Constellation is the name of an alleged unacknowledged special access program that entered public reporting in October 2024 through the journalist Michael Shellenberger and entered the Congressional Record on 13 November 2024. According to the whistleblower report Shellenberger delivered to the House Oversight Committee, it was created by the Department of Defense in 2017 after the New York Times published on AATIP, and functions as a central or parent USAP consolidating UAP observations from tasked and untasked collection platforms. The Department of Defense has stated it has no record of any such program.
entityDossier.whyImplicated: The allegation is not that a secret exists but that a specific legal mechanism was used to keep it from Congress. Shellenberger's sworn written testimony states that a source told him the SAP 'is controlled by the White House and executed and administrated by the DOD to avoid compliance with Title 10 of the United States Code', adding: 'It is essentially a DOD Program, as the White House directed the SECDEF to run it. But that's the loophole.' The same testimony identifies the statutes that should have compelled notification - 10 U.S.C. 119 and 50 U.S.C. 3093 - and asserts that the White House has a loophole for non-covert-action waived programs. That is a falsifiable structural claim about how a compartment can be run without triggering either SAP notification to the congressional defense committees or covert action findings to the intelligence committees. If true, it explains the entire pattern of this board: programmes that no oversight body can locate because no oversight body was ever the notification recipient.
entityDossier.narrative:
In October 2024 Michael Shellenberger, founder of the outlet Public, reported that a current or former US government official acting as a UAP whistleblower had provided him a report naming an active and highly secretive Department of Defense unacknowledged special access program. On 13 November 2024 he appeared under oath before the House Oversight Committee and the twelve-page document was entered into the Congressional Record from the dais.

His written testimony sets out the constitutional frame before it names anything. It cites 10 U.S.C. 119 and 50 U.S.C. 3093 - the SAP notification statute and the covert action statute - and states: 'DEPSECDEF must notify congress regarding DOD SAPs and the President must notify regarding Covert Action. For UAPs this is apparently not happening because the White House has a loophole for non-covert action waived programs.' The whistleblower's own words, as quoted in the testimony, are that 'the Executive Branch has been managing UAP/NHI issues without Congressional knowledge, oversight, or authorization for some time, quite possibly decades.'

The source characterisation of the programme is that it 'is a "strategic intelligence program" that is part of the US military's family of long-standing, highly-sensitive programs dealing with various aspects of the UAP "problem."' The report itself, as quoted in the testimony, says 'IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION serves as a central or "parent" USAP that consolidates observations' of UAPs 'by both tasked and untasked collection platforms.' It 'includes high-quality Imagery Intelligence (IMINT) and Measurement and Signature Intelligence (MASINT) of UAPs', drawn from 'a blend of directed and incidental collection capabilities positioned in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), the upper atmosphere' and at aviation and maritime altitudes. The most common shapes in the dataset are given as 'spheres/orbs, discs/saucers, ovals/tic-tacs, triangles, boomerang/arrowhead, and irregular/organic.'

The incident material is specific enough to be checkable by anyone with access to the underlying databases. One case: orbs surrounding and forcing an F-22 out of its patrol area, in which 'The F-22 broke trajectory and attempted to evade but was intercepted and boxed in by approximately 3-6 UAPs', with one UAP maintaining 'a rigid spatial relationship with the F-22, maintaining its exact position and orientation parallel with the F-22's cockpit despite multiple evasive rolls and maneuvers.' Another: the crew of a Navy aircraft carrier watching a 'small orange-red sphere' rapidly descend from high altitude to 100-200 yards directly above the flight deck. A third, sourced after publication: a roughly thirteen-minute high-definition full-colour video of a white orb emerging from the ocean approximately twenty miles off the coast of Kuwait, filmed from a helicopter, joined mid-video by a second orb, discovered by the source on SIPR.

The testimony also records a warning about the name itself. 'A source warned that simply printing the name "Immaculate Constellation" could trigger government surveillance of me under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) of whoever publishes it. "They won't comment on it, but talking about it will put you in the danger zone," I was told.' From the dais that day Rep. Nancy Mace said the same thing out loud: 'And Representative Luna just told me, if I say, "Immaculate Constellation," I will be on some list. Maybe a FISA warrant. So, come at me bro, I guess.'

The Department's response is a records assertion, and Shellenberger printed it in his own testimony: 'DOD spokesperson Sue Gough said, "The DOD has no record, present or historical, of any type of SAP called 'IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION.'"' That is not a statement that the programme does not exist. It is a statement about what a records search returned, made by a public affairs office that would not hold the read-on to an unacknowledged compartment. Mace's framing on the dais captured the structure exactly: '12 pages about this unacknowledged special access program that your government says does not exist.'

Two further items from the same hearing bear on the plausibility of the mechanism rather than the name. Retired Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet, formerly the Navy's chief meteorologist, testified: 'I concluded that the UAP information must have been classified within a special access program managed by an intelligence agency. That is, a compartmented program that even senior officials, including myself, were not read into.' And Luis Elizondo, asked directly by Mace whether he was read into secret UAP crash retrieval programmes, answered: 'We would have to have a conversation in a closed session, ma'am. I signed documentation 3 years ago that restricts my ability to discuss specifically crash retrievals.'

Under questioning from Rep. Clay Higgins, Shellenberger confirmed he knows the report's author - 'I do' - and declined to characterise the author's institutional position. Asked by Mace what the programme's mission is, he answered that it is an unacknowledged special access program whose 'mission is to document UAPs'. He also stated that when he checked the report against existing public cases he 'did not find it based on existing cases; it was new cases for me', which he offered as evidence against circular reporting.

What the record does not contain is any independent corroboration of the name from a second identified source, any document bearing the programme name, or any executive branch statement beyond the records denial. The name has never appeared in an AARO annual report, in any PURSUE tranche description, or in any published DoD product.
entityDossier.denialPosture: Department of Defense spokesperson Sue Gough is quoted in Shellenberger's written testimony as saying: 'The DOD has no record, present or historical, of any type of SAP called "IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION."' That is a records assertion rather than a denial of existence, and it is the standard formulation available to an office without read-on to an unacknowledged compartment. Rep. Mace characterised it from the dais as a programme 'that your government says does not exist'. No further departmental statement has been made in the twenty-one months since.
openQuestions: The identity and institutional position of the report's author, which Shellenberger confirmed he knows but declined to disclose.
Whether any congressional committee has formally requested a SAP notification search under 10 U.S.C. 119 against the alleged programme, and what the response was.
Whether the 'non-covert action waived program' loophole described in the testimony is a real category in current SAP practice, and which office administers such programmes.

Whether the specific incidents described - the F-22 boxing event, the CVN flight deck sphere, the Kuwait helicopter video on SIPR - correspond to identifiable case numbers in AARO, UAPTF or service databases.
No document bearing the programme name has ever been published; the only artefact in the public record is the twelve-page report entered by Rep. Mace.
Claims elsewhere that former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick denied the programme could not be verified against a primary source for this dossier and are not asserted here.

entityDossier.whatItIs: A twelve-page document that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress on the morning of 13 November 2024 and that Rep. Nancy Mace moved into the Congressional Record from the dais during the House Oversight Committee hearing 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth'. Its first section describes an unacknowledged special access program named Immaculate Constellation; its second section concerns United States Government imagery intelligence. It is listed in the hearing's Index of Documents as 'Report, Pentagon, "Immaculate Constellation"; submitted by Rep. Mace.'
entityDossier.whyImplicated: This is the only artefact in the entire public record that purports to be an internal description of a UAP parent compartment, and a chairwoman of a House committee put it into the Congressional Record while the Department of Defense was on record saying it has no record of the programme it names. The document is therefore a test case for the whole disclosure machinery: a congressional committee can receive, distribute to every member on the dais, and formally enter a document about an unacknowledged SAP, and nothing follows. No agency was compelled to search for it, no author was subpoenaed, no classification review was triggered, and no executive branch office has addressed its contents. It is the disclosure mechanism working exactly as designed and producing exactly nothing.
entityDossier.narrative:
The document arrived on the morning of the hearing. Rep. Mace flagged it in her opening remarks before the witnesses were sworn: 'there is a document that will be entered into the congressional record today. Mr. Tim Burchett from Tennessee has this document, and we just distributed it to every Member up here on the dais, this document. But this is going to be the original document from the Pentagon about Immaculate Constellation that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress today.' She then characterised it: '12 pages about this unacknowledged special access program that your government says does not exist.'

Later in the hearing, after the last of the opening statements, she performed the formal act: 'Committee staff asked me to go ahead, and I will do it, to enter into the Congressional Record this 12-page document that Michael Shellenberger brought today that describes the Immaculate Constellation government program. So, we will do that now. Every Member up here has a copy of it.' She then described its structure on the record: 'The first section talks about the unacknowledged special access program called Immaculate Constellation, and the second section about USG imagery intelligence.' She added the FISA warning she had just received from Rep. Luna, and closed with 'But, without objection, entered into the record.'

The printed hearing record's Index of Documents lists it as 'Report, Pentagon, "Immaculate Constellation"; submitted by Rep. Mace', alongside a Mellon hearing letter submitted by Mace, documents related to UAPs submitted by Burchett, and Questions for the Record to Elizondo, Gallaudet, Shellenberger and Gold submitted by Burlison. The record states that 'The documents listed above are available at: docs.house.gov.'

The contents, as read into the record by Shellenberger in his oral statement and set out at greater length in his written testimony, are consistent between the two. The report describes a parent USAP consolidating UAP observations from tasked and untasked collection platforms; a holdings profile of high-quality IMINT and MASINT from low Earth orbit, the upper atmosphere, aviation altitudes and maritime environments; a shape taxonomy of spheres and orbs, discs and saucers, ovals and tic-tacs, triangles, boomerang and arrowhead forms and irregular or organic shapes; and seven categories of evidence. The written testimony says the report 'describes in detail various UAP sightings collected by technical assets and US military personnel', and that the underlying material sits in defence HUMINT databases 'accessible to the Intelligence Community'.

Two incident descriptions are quoted directly from the report in the written testimony. The F-22 encounter: 'The F-22 broke trajectory and attempted to evade but was intercepted and boxed in by approximately 3-6 UAPs', with one object holding station off the cockpit through multiple evasive manoeuvres before the aircraft 'was forced out of the mission area under the escort of the UAP formation.' And the carrier deck event, in which a small orange-red sphere descended from high altitude to within 100-200 yards directly above the flight deck of a CVN.

The evidentiary character of the document is worth stating plainly, because the argument does not need it inflated. It is an anonymous report, delivered by a journalist, whose author Shellenberger says he knows and will not name. Under questioning from Rep. Higgins he confirmed 'I do' when asked whether he knew the author, and when pressed on the author's sources referred back to the report itself. He offered one internal check: that when he compared its cases against publicly known cases he 'did not find it based on existing cases; it was new cases for me', which he presented as an argument against circular reporting. That is a weak check, and he said so in effect by presenting it as the only one he could make.

What gives the document its standing is not its provenance but its position. It sits in the Congressional Record. It was distributed to every member on the dais of a House committee. It names a compartment. And the executive branch response to it, before and since, has been a single sentence from a public affairs office - Sue Gough's statement that 'The DOD has no record, present or historical, of any type of SAP called "IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION"' - which addresses records holdings and not existence, and which was itself printed in the witness's own testimony rather than issued in response to the congressional entry.

Since 13 November 2024 the document has been followed by nothing. No agency has confirmed conducting a search. No committee has published a referral. No classification authority has asserted that the document is classified, which would be the ordinary response to an authentic Pentagon report on an unacknowledged SAP appearing in a public hearing room; nor has any authority asserted that it is a forgery, which would be the ordinary response to a fabrication. That double silence is the most interesting fact about the artefact. The disclosure machinery accepted the document and then had nowhere to put it, because the mechanism Congress built in 2023 - a records collection administered by the agencies that hold the records - has no procedure for a document that arrives from outside the agencies and describes a compartment the agencies say they cannot find.

entityDossier.whatItIs: The PURSUE releases are the five dated tranches of UAP material published by the Department of War at war.gov/UFO between 8 May 2026 and 7 August 2026. Each tranche is posted as a paired download - a document bundle served from www.war.gov/medialink/ufo/ and a video bundle served from a CloudFront distribution - alongside a searchable database of individual records. The files carry originator-prefixed identifiers such as DOW-UAP-D###, DOW-UAP-PR## and FBI-UAP-D###, the first time the United States Government has issued UAP material under a single public numbering scheme.
entityDossier.whyImplicated: This is the physical evidence of what the government chose to hand over when a President ordered it to hand something over. The ledger is therefore diagnostic in both directions. It confirms the archive: material spanning 1944 to 2026, FBI holdings, NASA crew audio, INDOPACOM reporting, all of it previously unavailable and now released without clearance. It also confirms the shape of the withholding: at least a hundred of the roughly 160 files in the first tranche carry redactions, and every serious analyst who examined them - Mellon, Graves, Gallaudet, Rojas - reported the same absence of coordinates, sensor parameters, altitude, timing and chain of custody, which are the precise fields that would permit independent verification. No tranche carries a manifest, an exemption citation, a FOIA case number or a provenance statement. The releases are the strongest available proof that the holdings exist and the strongest available proof that the release process was designed to be unauditable.
entityDossier.narrative:
Five tranches, over three months, from a Department web page. Release 01 on 8 May 2026, Release 02 on 22 May, Release 03 on 12 June, Release 04 on 10 July, Release 05 on 7 August. The portal states the sequence plainly: 'The Department of War just released the fifth tranche of records under PURSUE. The first tranche was released on May 8, 2026.'

The delivery mechanism is worth describing exactly, because it is not a records system. Each release offers two ZIP archives. The documents come from war.gov itself: Release 01 documents at 1.2gb, Release 02 at 70.1mb, Release 03 at 826mb, Release 04 at 227mb, Release 05 at 130mb. The videos come from a commercial content delivery network at d34w7g4gy10iej.cloudfront.net: 1.3gb, 5.6gb, 4.6gb, 1.4gb and 513mb respectively. There is no manifest file, no checksum, no metadata schema, no index of what was withheld. The portal offers a filterable database by agency, release, incident date, incident location and type - which is more structure than any prior US UAP release has had, and still less than any archivist would call a finding aid. At the time this dossier was compiled the portal's 'LATEST RELEASE' link still pointed to Release 04 while the banner above it announced Release 05, which tells you something about how the page is maintained.

The file identifiers are the most analytically useful artefact in the whole programme. Filenames visible on the portal include DOW-UAP-PR46-Unresolved-UAP-Report-INDOPACOM-2024, DOW-UAP-D098_Film-Analysis-of-Unidentified-Objects_1953, FBI-UAP-D025_Digital-Rendering_Airborne-Triangle_2002, FBI-UAP-D027_Digital-Rendering_Dark-Translucent-Triangle_2023, FBI-UAP-D031_Digital-Rendering_Large-Triangle-with-Red-Lights_2023 and FBI-UAP-D038 through D042, a run of digital renderings of multiple red lights dated 2026. Two things follow. First, the numbering is originator-prefixed, which means the tranches were assembled by pulling from multiple agencies' holdings under a single tasking rather than compiled from one department's files - a single-department dump would not need agency prefixes. Second, the Bureau is a substantial contributor, and its contributions run to the present: FBI-UAP-D038 through D042 are dated 2026, the year of release.

The imagery convention is itself a disclosure decision. A large share of the FBI material is published as 'Digital Rendering' - artists' reconstructions of witness accounts rather than sensor products. DefenseScoop's illustration caption for the first tranche describes an 'Actual site photo with FBI rendered graphic depicting corroborating eye witness reports from September 2023 of an apparent ellipsoid bronze metallic object materializing out of a bright light in the sky, 130-195 feet in length, and disappearing instantaneously.' A rendering cannot be independently analysed. It can only be believed or not.

On volume and redaction, the contemporaneous count is DefenseScoop's: 'The initial PURSUE tranche contained a little more than 160 files, with at least 100 of those including redactions, according to researchers and experts who are currently studying them.' Roughly five files in eight were released with material removed, in a programme whose stated purpose was to stop hiding material, and with no exemption citation attached to any redaction.

The substantive verdict from the people best placed to give one was delivered within a week and was unanimous on the technical point. Alejandro Rojas, whose Enigma Labs team was cross-referencing the drop against a database of over 200,000 public sightings: 'Although there is a lot of information here, there is little context. Case summaries without coordinates, sensor parameters, or altitude data make independent analysis very difficult.' Tim Gallaudet, who thought some of the videos showed genuinely anomalous behaviour including right-angle turns and formation flying: 'the ambiguity of the video content in particular is concerning as no metadata was included. Therefore, it is impossible to conclude that any of the objects were truly anomalous.' Ryan Graves, on what a useful release looks like: 'The real value is in records that include clear provenance, sensor context, metadata, chain of custody, date and location, and enough operational context to allow serious independent analysis. Ambiguous imagery without that surrounding data is hard for pilots, researchers, or the public to evaluate responsibly.'

Several of the same people noted that much of the first tranche was not new. The Australian researcher Grant Lavac: 'For those of us in the UAP research community, the newness of the data in this first tranche is underwhelming. Much of it is a compilation of documents that have been in the public domain for decades.' His countervailing point is the one this board accepts: 'the story here isn't necessarily the content, but the process of official acknowledgment.'

And there is a provenance problem that the releases themselves create. Jordan Flowers of the Disclosure Foundation raised it in the first week: the US Government's own documented mid-century practice of manufacturing false UAP documents as cover for real weapons programmes means some of what is being published as authentic government UAP records may be disinformation artefacts. 'If some of what is now being released to the public as authentic government UAP records are in fact disinformation artifacts from that era, the public deserves to know. Transparency requires not just releasing files, but accounting for their provenance and integrity.' PURSUE publishes without provenance statements, which means it cannot distinguish a genuine 1953 film analysis from a 1953 cover story, and neither can anyone downstream.

What the ledger establishes is therefore narrower and harder than the headlines suggested. The archive exists and is large. The Department was able to produce material from at least six agencies within eleven weeks of a presidential post. The material released is the unresolved residue, stripped of the fields that would let anyone check it, with a third to two-thirds of it redacted and none of it assessed. That is not the record of a government that has nothing. It is the record of a government deciding, file by file, how much of what it has to show.

claims.text: The war.gov/UFO portal states: 'The Department of War just released the fifth tranche of records under PURSUE. The first tranche was released on May 8, 2026. Scroll down to view the fifth tranche, released on Aug. 7, 2026.'
Each release is published as a paired download: document bundles hosted at www.war.gov/medialink/ufo/ and video bundles hosted at the CloudFront distribution d34w7g4gy10iej.cloudfront.net.

Published bundle sizes are: Release 01 documents 1.2gb and videos 1.3gb; Release 02 documents 70.1mb and videos 5.6gb; Release 03 documents 826mb and videos 4.6gb; Release 04 documents 227mb and videos 1.4gb; Release 05 documents 130mb and videos 513mb.

Released files carry originator-prefixed identifiers. Filenames published on the portal include DOW-UAP-PR46-Unresolved-UAP-Report-INDOPACOM-2024, DOW-UAP-D098_Film-Analysis-of-Unidentified-Objects_1953, and FBI-UAP-D025, D027, D029, D031 and D038 through D042.

The Release 05 slideshow published on the portal consists largely of FBI 'Digital Rendering' images of triangular and multi-light objects dated 2002, 2011, 2023 and 2026, alongside a 1953 Department of War film analysis item.

The portal's release database is filterable by agency, release, incident date, incident location and file type, but publishes no manifest, checksum, metadata schema, FOIA case number, exemption citation or provenance statement for any tranche.
At the time of compilation the portal's 'LATEST RELEASE' link pointed to release=04 while the banner above it announced Release 05 of 7 August 2026.

DefenseScoop reported: 'The initial PURSUE tranche contained a little more than 160 files, with at least 100 of those including redactions, according to researchers and experts who are currently studying them.'

Alejandro Rojas of Enigma Labs, whose team cross-referenced the drop against a database of over 200,000 public sightings, said: 'Although there is a lot of information here, there is little context. Case summaries without coordinates, sensor parameters, or altitude data make independent analysis very difficult.'

Ryan Graves said of the releases: 'The most useful releases are not simply the clips that appear unusual. The real value is in records that include clear provenance, sensor context, metadata, chain of custody, date and location, and enough operational context to allow serious independent analysis.'

Researcher Grant Lavac said of the first tranche: 'For those of us in the UAP research community, the newness of the data in this first tranche is underwhelming. Much of it is a compilation of documents that have been in the public domain for decades', but that 'the story here isn't necessarily the content, but the process of official acknowledgment.'

Disclosure Foundation Executive Director Jordan Flowers raised a provenance-integrity problem with the releases: 'If some of what is now being released to the public as authentic government UAP records are in fact disinformation artifacts from that era, the public deserves to know. Transparency requires not just releasing files, but accounting for their provenance and integrity.'

Flowers also identified as notable in the first tranche 'The video of an object in Greece making multiple 90-degree turns at approximately 80 miles per hour' and 'The FBI orb reports from 2023, including the "Eye of Sauron" description witnessed by multiple teams from varying locations over two days', and imagery and reports captured by NASA astronauts on Apollo 12 and Apollo 17.

The originator-prefixed numbering scheme indicates the tranches were assembled by pulling from multiple agencies' holdings under a single presidential tasking rather than compiled from one department's files, since a single-department release would not require agency prefixes.

claims.text: The Department of War publishes the programme under the title 'Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE)' at war.gov/UFO.

The portal reproduces the presidential direction, dated 19 February 2026 and attributed to Truth Social: 'Based on the tremendous interest shown, I will be directing the Secretary of War, and other relevant Departments and Agencies, to begin the process of identifying and releasing Government files related to alien and extraterrestrial life, unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP), and unidentified flying objects (UFOs), and any and all other information connected to these highly complex, but extremely interesting and important, matters. GOD BLESS AMERICA!'

The portal's Directive states that the Department of War, 'with support from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), is overseeing government wide efforts to expeditiously find, review, identify, declassify and publicly release unresolved UAP-related records', an undertaking 'that requires coordination between dozens of agencies and the review of tens of millions of records, many existing only on paper, spanning many decades', with 'tranches posted every few weeks.'

The portal limits the collection's scope: 'The materials archived here are unresolved cases, meaning the government is unable to make a definitive determination on the nature of the observed phenomena', and states 'DOW will continue to conduct separate reporting on resolved UAP cases, as mandated by statute.'

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth's published statement reads: 'The Department of War is in lockstep with President Trump to bring unprecedented transparency regarding our government's understanding of Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena. These files, hidden behind classifications, have long fueled justified speculation - and it's time the American people see it for themselves.'

The 8 May 2026 Department of War release names the interagency participants as 'The White House, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), the Department of Energy (DOE), the DOW's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and additional components of U.S. intelligence agencies.'
The same release concedes: 'While all of the files have been reviewed for security purposes, many of the materials have not yet been analyzed for resolution of any anomalies.'

Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard's statement describes ODNI as 'actively coordinating the Intelligence Community's declassification efforts with the Department of War to ensure a careful, comprehensive, and unprecedented review of our holdings', and calls the 8 May release 'the first in what will be an ongoing joint declassification and release effort.'

A War Department official told DefenseScoop: 'AARO is responsible for coordinating the declassification of identified DOW files. AARO also prepares DOW files and files provided by other agencies for posting on war.gov/ufo. AARO will continue to conduct its statutory mission of detecting, identifying, analyzing, and resolving UAP. Any encounters described in these releases that are resolved in the future will be posted on aaro.mil.'

DefenseScoop reported on 14 May 2026 that PURSUE tranches are 'dropping on the new, centralized war.gov/ufo portal - not the existing aaro.mil website', and identified the acronym expansion as the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters.

A War Department official stated the programme's editorial posture: 'We are not providing any comment or assessment on the files overall or on any specific file, so that the American people can make up their own minds regarding the files.'

Christopher Mellon, former deputy assistant secretary of defense for intelligence, said of the first tranche: 'For years the public was told there was little to see. The scale of what exists is itself a revelation. That said, data alone is not disclosure. Releasing raw files without context may confuse more than clarify.' He added that 'it is releasing evidence without releasing analysis.'
The war.gov/UFO portal's 'Learn More' section directs readers seeking 'other historical UAP records' to aaro.mil, the statutory office's site, which is not the host of the PURSUE material.

PURSUE is not a statutory declassification process, not a FOIA channel and not the National Archives UAP Records Collection created by Public Law 118-31; it is a departmental publication programme run on the Secretary's web estate under a presidential direction announced on social media.

entityDossier.denialPosture: The Department of War declines to characterise its own releases: a War Department official told DefenseScoop 'We are not providing any comment or assessment on the files overall or on any specific file, so that the American people can make up their own minds regarding the files.' No exemption authority has been cited for any redaction, and no official has responded to the uniform expert finding that the released material lacks the metadata required for independent analysis.
openQuestions: Per-tranche file counts and composition are reported by third-party inventories rather than by any official manifest; the Department has published no authoritative count for any release.
Under what authority the redactions in at least 100 first-tranche files were applied, and whether any withholding log exists.

Whether an ODNI-prefixed identifier series (ODNI-UAP-D###) exists in the released material; DOW- and FBI-prefixed identifiers are directly verifiable on the portal, ODNI-prefixed ones were not verified for this dossier.
Whether any released video retains embedded sensor metadata in the source files as distinct from the portal case summaries.
How the Department distinguishes authentic historical records from mid-century disinformation artefacts before publication, if it does so at all.
Whether any material relating to recovery, custody or reverse engineering was within the scope of the PURSUE search, and whether any such material was found and withheld.
No executive order, memorandum or written tasking implementing the 19 February 2026 direction has been published; the legal instrument governing PURSUE is not on the public record.
What search terms, record series and agency components were tasked, and whether special access program holdings were within scope at all.
Which office adjudicates redactions and under which exemption authority, given that no FOIA case numbers or exemption citations appear on the released material.
Whether the Department of Energy's participation extends to Restricted Data or transclassified foreign nuclear information holdings, the exemption route the Senate identified in 2023.
Whether any records were withheld in full, and whether a withholding log exists.
Whether AARO's preparation role gives it the ability to exclude material originated by other DoW components before posting.
